h1. Unified Inference — PRD, Design, Roadmap & Pricing (v14)

Summary:
This document consolidates the product requirements, high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing updates, and release notes for Unified Inference v14. v14 focuses on predictable latency at scale, new cost controls for multi-tenant workloads, and a simplified tiered pricing model that aligns with Dedicated and Private offerings.

Purpose and audience:
This page is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders who need a single reference for scope, timeline, and commercial changes for the v14 release.

## Goals
- Deliver 99th percentile latency SLO improvements for small and medium request sizes by 20% on average across hosted regions.
- Reduce per-token cost for common request patterns via improved KV caching and adaptive batching.
- Launch a simplified three-tier pricing model for Redwood API (Self-serve, Dedicated Starter, Enterprise) with clear migration paths.
- Expose new routing controls (region / cost / latency) in the API and Console.

## Success metrics (targeted)
- 99th percentile text-generation latency <= 450ms for requests <= 512 tokens (hosted API).
- 15% reduction in per-token GPU cost for top 20% of workloads within three months of rollout.
- Self-serve conversion rate (trial -> paying) increase by 8% attributable to pricing simplification.
- Net Promoter Score (NPS) for enterprise pilots >= 55.

## Personas
- ML/Platform engineer integrating Redwood API into product services.
- Product engineer optimizing end-user latency and costs.
- Platform architect evaluating Dedicated or Private deployment options.

## Problem statement
Teams building LLM features face unpredictable per-token costs and latency variance as load grows. Existing controls (manual batching, model pinning) are powerful but fragmented. Customers ask for: (a) clearer pricing that maps to expected latency/cost tradeoffs, (b) programmatic routing controls, and (c) automatic cost optimizations without sacrificing SLOs.

## Scope
In-scope:
- API extensions for routing and priority hints.
- Console UX for tier-based cost controls and per-route profiles.
- Runtime improvements: adaptive batching, smarter KV cache heuristics, and kernel selection adjustments for medium-length sequences.
- Pricing model: public documentation, billing changes, and migration tooling.

Out-of-scope (v14):
- New model training or model versioning marketplace.
- Major rewrites to Dedicated autoscaling policies (incremental tuning only).

## Requirements
Functional requirements (FR)
1. FR-1: API: Add optional request routing fields to the generation endpoint: routing_policy (latency|cost|region), priority_hint (low|normal|high). Documented in SDKs and REST docs.
2. FR-2: Console: Per-route profile editor with sliders for cost/latency targets and visible estimate of unit economics.
3. FR-3: Runtime: Implement adaptive batching that maintains latency SLOs and reverts batch sizes for high-priority requests.
4. FR-4: Billing: New billing meter for routing-tier adjustments and per-route caching credits.

Non-functional requirements (NFR)
1. NFR-1: Backwards compatibility for existing API clients; default routing_policy should be "latency" for existing clients.
2. NFR-2: Security: routing metadata must be logged with tenant isolation and forwarded to audit logs.
3. NFR-3: Observability: metrics and traces for routing decisions must be exposed in Console and telemetry.
4. NFR-4: Performance: changes to runtime must not increase 50th percentile latency by >5% at baseline load.

## Design overview
High-level approach:
- Client-side: SDKs add routing_policy and priority_hint to request payloads.
- Control-plane: Console persists per-route profiles; pricing tier is mapped to a routing policy template.
- Serving runtime: Request router evaluates policy, consults cached KV prefixes, and selects execution path with adaptive batching.

Architecture components:
- API Gateway: validates routing fields and forwards to Smart Router.
- Smart Router: policy engine that chooses model variant, region, and queue priority.
- Batch Manager: maintains per-worker batching windows and preemptive slots for high-priority requests.
- KV Cache Coordinator: global prefix cache with tenant-safe eviction heuristics.

Example API contract (generation request):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-3b",
  "input": "Summarize the following...",
  "routing_policy": "cost",
  "priority_hint": "normal",
  "route_id": "customer-analytics-api"
}
```

Design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Adaptive batching improves cost efficiency but can increase tail latency for high-power bursts; to mitigate, we provide explicit priority_hint and allow per-route canaries.
- Global KV caching reduces token compute but increases cross-tenant memory pressure; eviction is tenant-aware and configurable per Dedicated/Private deployments.

## Observability & SLOs
|| Metric || Target || Alert threshold || Owner ||
|| 99th percentile generation latency (<=512 tokens) || <= 450ms || > 550ms for 5m || eng-serving-runtime ||
|| Average per-token GPU cost (hosted) || -15% vs v13 baseline || > -5% improvement over 14 days || eng-sre ||
|| Route-level error rate || < 0.5% || > 1% for 5m || eng-platform ||

Required dashboards and telemetry:
- Per-route latency/cost heatmaps (Console).
- Smart Router decision logs with sampling.
- Batch Manager window size histogram.

## Roadmap & themes (Q2 2027 – Q4 2027)
- Q2 2027 (v14 GA): Core routing API, Console route profiles, adaptive batching rollout to hosted regions, pricing model public launch.
- Q3 2027: Dedicated Starter tier launch, migration tooling for committed customers, advanced KV cache diagnostics.
- Q4 2027: Private deployment support for routing templates and offline billing reconciliation; enterprise SLAs for routing latency.

Milestones and release cadence:
1. 2027-03-01: PRD sign-off (this document).
2. 2027-03-15: API contract freeze and SDK changes merged.
3. 2027-04-10: Smart Router PoC complete (internal).
4. 2027-05-20: Canary in prod (5% traffic).
5. 2027-06-15: GA release and pricing switch.

## Pricing & Packaging changes
Rationale: Simplify purchasing decisions and align per-unit economics with the operational levers we expose (batching, cache, routing).
New tiers:
- Self-serve (pay-as-you-go): baseline per-token pricing, limited routing features, per-route caching disabled by default.
- Dedicated Starter (reserved capacity): discounted per-token rates, per-route caching enabled, predictable throughput up to committed units.
- Enterprise: custom pricing, advanced routing templates, extended retention, and dedicated support.

Pricing table (illustrative list):
|| Tier || Per-token (generation) || Embedding/unit || Notes ||
|| Self-serve || $0.0009 / token || $0.0004 / embed || No per-route caching (can be enabled at cost) ||
|| Dedicated Starter || $0.00055 / token || $0.00025 / embed || Requires monthly commit; includes basic routing templates ||
|| Enterprise || Custom || Custom || SLA-backed, advanced features ||

Migration plan for existing customers:
1. Notify affected customers 60 days prior to switch with per-customer impact report.
2. Offer a 90-day migration credit for high-use accounts.
3. Provide tooling to simulate v14 billing under new tiers in Console.

Billing implementation notes:
- Introduce a new billing dimension: routing_tier_credit.
- Track per-route cache credits and surface them in billing UI.

## Release notes (v14)
Highlights:
- New request fields: routing_policy and priority_hint.
- Console: route profiles and cost/latency estimator.
- Runtime: adaptive batching and improved KV cache heuristics.
- Pricing: public launch of three-tier model and migration tooling.

Behavioral changes for users:
- Default behaviour remains the same; existing clients will not see changes unless they opt into routing fields or route profiles.
- Observability: additional logs and metrics will appear under route-level dashboards.

Known limitations and workarounds:
- Very large batch windows (>2048 tokens average) may briefly increase 99th percentile latency during heavy burst traffic. Workaround: set priority_hint=high for latency-sensitive requests.
- Per-route caching is CPU/memory intensive for multi-tenant shared pools; recommend Dedicated Starter for heavy cache usage.

## Rollout plan and operational checklist
Pre-release (engineering & SRE)
- [ ] API contract freeze and SDK updates published.
- [ ] Automated load tests covering routing_policy permutations.
- [ ] Canary pipeline configured (5% traffic, region-aware).

Canary (production)
- Duration: 2 weeks minimum
- Monitoring: 99th/95th latency, per-route error rate, GPU utilization, billing delta.
- Rollback criteria: sustained >10% regression in 99th latency or >1% increase in error rate for 15 minutes.

GA
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 14 days with load-based throttling.
- Sales enablement: updated pricing docs, migration guides, sample customer impact reports.
- Customer success: dedicated outreach to top 50 high-usage accounts.

## Appendix
Compatibility matrix:
- Self-serve SDKs: v2.4+ (JS, Python) required for routing_policy fields.
- Dedicated: minor runtime upgrade (no infra change) for Dedicated Starter; scheduled during maintenance window.

Example per-route JSON profile (Console export):
```
{
  "route_id": "customer-analytics-api",
  "routing_template": "cost-optimized",
  "priority_defaults": "normal",
  "cache_enabled": true,
  "est_cost_delta": "-12%"
}
```

Next steps:
1. Finalize API spec and publish SDK changes (due 2027-03-15).
2. Coordinate billing implementation with finance for new billing dimensions (due 2027-04-01).
3. Start canary rollout and monitor metrics (due 2027-05-20).
